title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
abstract:
Nature Medicine, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04756-1

As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In a 5 year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen with high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.
headline: Adding a second immune-boosting drug to melanoma treatment improves survival for patients with specific immune markers.
why_it_matters: Melanoma is one of the deadliest cancers, and this 5-year study shows a combination therapy works better than a single drug for some patients. More importantly, researchers identified a biological marker (LAG3 high CD8+ T cells) that predicts who will benefit most, moving us toward personalized cancer treatment.
key_findings: The combination of relatlimab (a new drug) plus nivolumab (an existing immunotherapy) outperformed nivolumab alone in extending both progression-free survival (time before cancer worsens) and overall survival (time until death).

Patients whose tumors had high baseline levels of LAG3 high CD8+ T cells (immune cells with a specific marker) responded best to the combination therapy, suggesting this biomarker (biological sign) could help doctors choose which patients benefit most.
These survival benefits held up over 5 years of follow-up, indicating the improvement was durable and not just a short-term effect.
Melanoma-specific survival (time until death from melanoma specifically) also improved with the combination, showing the drugs were actually controlling the cancer, not just other health factors.
methods_snapshot: Researchers followed melanoma patients from a large phase 3 clinical trial (the gold standard for testing new drugs) who received either nivolumab alone or nivolumab plus relatlimab, tracking their survival and analyzing their immune cells over 5 years. They looked for biological markers in tumor samples that predicted which patients would respond best to each treatment.

glossary.definition: A deadly form of skin cancer that starts in pigment-producing cells and can spread throughout the body.
Cancer treatment that harnesses the body's own immune system to find and kill cancer cells.
An FDA-approved immunotherapy drug that blocks a protein cancer cells use to hide from the immune system.
A newer immunotherapy drug that removes a different 'brake' on immune cells, allowing them to fight cancer more effectively.
A specific type of immune fighter cell with a marker called LAG3; high numbers of these cells suggest the patient's immune system is primed to respond to the combination therapy.
A measurable biological sign (like a protein or cell type) in the body or tumor that helps predict treatment response or disease prognosis.
The length of time a patient lives without their cancer getting worse.
The length of time a patient lives from the start of treatment, regardless of cause of death.

limitations: This study enrolled patients who met specific criteria, so results may not apply equally to all melanoma patients; additionally, the biomarker analysis (LAG3 high CD8+ T cells) requires validation in independent patient populations to confirm its predictive power.
